Common-wealth this measure is false: Not the Appetite
of Private men, but the Law, which is the Will and
Appetite of the State is the measure. And yet is this
Doctrine still practised ; and men judge the Goodnesse,
or Wickednesse of their own, and of other mens actions,
_ and of the actions of the Common-wealth it selfe, by
their own Passions ; and no man calleth Good or Evill,
but that which is so in his own eyes, without any regard
at all to the Publique Laws; except onely Monks, and
Friers, that are bound by Vow to that simple obedience
to their Superiour, to which every Subject ought to
think himself bound by the Law of Nature to the Civill
Soveraign. And this private measure of Good, is a Doc-
trine, not onely Vain, but also Pernicious to the Publique
State.
